decisionThisFileRecords.id: WFC-004 DECISION 1 — the canonical home for vendor identity, and the explicit decision NOT to create two of the six names live code reads
decisionThisFileRecords.decided: The canonical vendor identity home is a NEW table `public.vendor_entities`, plus `public.vendor_entity_aliases` as the real target for VendorMergePlan.aliasesToRetain. It is deliberately NOT named `vendors` and NOT named `org_vendors`.
decisionThisFileRecords.evidenceForTheShape: Exactly one vendor table in this repository has a reviewed ADR (docs/admin-feature-specs/adr/VEND-102-vendor-identity-deduplication.md), a tested pure implementation (lib/admin/vendor-identity.ts, 354 lines + 143-line test), archived DDL and a verify function. `VendorIdentityRecord` (:93-109) matches that archived DDL FIELD FOR FIELD, and `planVendorMerge.aliasesToRetain` (:292-346) returns rows whose shape is exactly the archived `vendor_aliases` columns. The contract is load-bearing TypeScript whose storage was never written. `buildVendorIdentityRow`, `planVendorMerge` and `findVendorDuplicateMatches` have zero production callers - only the test - so the storage gap is real and not merely unused.
decisionThisFileRecords.evidenceForTheName_provenByExecution: `app/api/admin/vendors/route.ts:21` selects `id, organization_id, name, vendor_type, rating, created_at, updated_at`. Against the VEND-102 shape that select raises SQLSTATE 42703 `column "organization_id" does not exist` - MEASURED, not inferred. 42703 is not 42P01, so the route's `if (error.code === "42P01")` at :31 does not fire; the outer catch's `msg.includes("relation") && msg.includes("does not exist")` at :56 also does not fire, because a 42703 message contains "does not exist" but NOT "relation" (a 42P01 message does: `relation "public.org_vendors" does not exist`). The route would therefore return 503 'Vendors unavailable' instead of today's `{success:true, vendors:[], unavailable:true, unavailableReason:"Vendors table not yet migrated."}`, which components/admin/vendors/vendor-master-panel.tsx:58-108 already reads and which is the ONLY CP-098-correct reader of the seven. Creating `vendors` here would convert the one honest degraded signal in this set into an outage signal.
decisionThisFileRecords.noCandidateSatisfiesTheLiveReader: Measured column by column. VEND-102 `vendors` satisfies 3 of the reader's 7 (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`); archived `logistics_vendors` (20260605100000) satisfies 5 of 7 but disagrees on the tenant key (`org_id`, not `organization_id`) and has no `rating`. `rating` exists in NO archived vendor table. Supplying the four missing names would mean creating a SECOND tenant key on the vendor master - the exact "five competing nullable tenant keys" defect WFC-003 §1.2 records on staff_members.
decisionThisFileRecords.recordedAsUNRESOLVED: `vendors` vs `org_vendors` is STILL not decided, and the repository cannot decide it. The two READERS demand mutually exclusive tenant column names for the same relation name (organization_id vs org_id), so if both names are real DDL on some target they cannot be one table - that is a statement about readers. Neither name has any DDL in this repository, so there is no entity evidence. DB-002 recorded that some hosted versions were applied by raw Management API SQL, so a target may hold either. `org_vendors`'s reader asks for 5 of the 7 values of the VEND-102 status CHECK, while archived `logistics_vendors` has no status column and `vendor_contracts.status` is {draft,active,expired,cancelled} and `event_vendor_requests.status` is {pending,confirmed,declined,cancelled}: three incompatible vocabularies. NO view named `org_vendors` or `vendors` is created either, because a view under either name would RATIFY the merge CP-096 forbids.
decisionThisFileRecords.whatWouldSettleIt: ONE read-only query on any real target: `select n.nspname, c.relname, c.relkind from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace where c.relname in ('vendors','org_vendors','vendor_compliance_documents','org_contracts','contract_signature_envelopes','vendor_aliases') order by 1,2;`. relkind 'v' for org_vendors means a projection decision and 'r' means an entity decision, which answers the merge question outright. If the merge is confirmed, the remedy is a 3-line column-limited view; if it is refuted, two distinct entities are needed and only then should a second vendor master be authored.
decisionThisFileRecords.noLiveRouteReadsItYet: Stated rather than left implied. No live route reads vendor_entities, and that is a consequence of the deferred merge decision, not an oversight. Consumers: WFC-005 and WFC-018 (vendor departments), DB-012 (vendor-to-organization ownership), ORG-007 (canonical vendor services), and lib/admin/vendor-identity.ts (VEND-102), whose buildVendorIdentityRow now has a table to write to. staffing_agencies (20250812090500:20-26) is a vendor-company-adjacent table with NO tenant column at all; it is NOT adopted, and 20260927100200 quarantines it as vendor_identity_name_only, which is WFC-003 §5 item 14's disposition and not a merge.
decisionThisFileRecords.routedTo: HF-DB-012-VENDOR-ENTITY-MERGE-UNRESOLVED (DB-012 and the vendor-domain owner). DB-012 must not proceed to author vendor-to-organization ownership on an undecided entity home.

assumptions: `vendor.view` and `vendor.manage` are in NO role's `org_role_permissions` row. They are in the org_members.permissions CHECK vocabulary (20260821180438:89) but not in the five roles the chain seeds (20250816132000:44-49, 20260712005429:219-235) and not in DB-016's workforce slice (20260926200000, which is workforce.* only, by WFC-003 §2.5's rule). MEASURED on the extracted matrix with DB-016 applied verbatim: has_perm(admin, org, 'vendor.view') is FALSE. So these policies deny an organization administrator. That is FAIL CLOSED, not a disclosure, and it is NOT fixed here: seeding vendor.* is a WFC-003 matrix decision under CP-102, and DB-016 established that ANY org_role_permissions write invalidates every active acting-context session because capability_version digests perms IN ORDER (20260722002848:180-183,317-320). The working path today is the per-member org_members.permissions array, which has_perm unions, and the harness MEASURES it: a member whose array carries vendor.view reads their organization's vendor entities, and the same organization's `admin` reads zero.

The archived VEND-102 `public.can_vendor` helper is deliberately NOT recreated. It is not in the chain, and introducing it would be a second parallel authority path - the CP-110 failure shape. These policies call the chain's own public.has_perm, the same function and the same two permissions that 20260720020544_admin_tour_collaboration_security.sql:180-207 already uses to gate tour collaboration on vendor.view / vendor.manage.

The column contract of the VEND-102 shape is adopted verbatim rather than re-derived, because the TypeScript that produces rows for it is live and tested. If a future lane decides the contract is wrong, the correction belongs in lib/admin/vendor-identity.ts and VEND-102's ADR together, not in a migration that silently reshapes the columns.

The `category` vocabulary is VEND-102's EIGHT values (lib/admin/vendor-identity.ts:8-17), not the SIXTEEN-value VendorCategory vocabulary in lib/admin/vendor-domain.ts:23-26. WFC-003 §5 item 15 records the two as not reconcilable by inference, so only the eight-value one is enforced here and the other is preserved untouched in the application. A vendor whose category is a sixteen-value-only value cannot be written until a human decides which vocabulary is canonical - recorded, not worked around.

`authenticated` must hold table-level SELECT on public.organizations and USAGE on schema auth. Both are Supabase defaults that this chain does not manage in SQL, both are invisible in this repository, and both were MEASURED as required by the harness rather than assumed. The first is DB-013's recorded surprise (:452-457) and is inherited knowingly; the second is NEW to this program, because the self-keyed policy arms in 20260927100100/200 call auth.uid() in CALLER context, unlike the auth.uid() inside has_perm/is_org_member which is SECURITY DEFINER. Without either grant the policies DENY (fail closed, never open) and the symptom is a functional false-denial. Both are labelled preflight probes with stop conditions, not assumptions this lane can discharge.

Every existing row is preserved. No pre-existing relation is created, altered or dropped; no pre-existing column is touched; no pre-existing data row is read for update or deleted. NO `information_schema.tables` existence guard appears anywhere in this file, so the CP-109 ordering trap is not reachable: both relations are created in this same file at a version later than anything that references them. `node supabase/tests/wfc004_guarded_block_order.mjs` measures that absence against the real 315-migration chain, and its self-test proves the instrument can fail (it must find the chain's 12 never-executed guards, including 20250812093500 over staff_performance_metrics).

lib/database.types.ts is byte-unchanged and this migration DOES require a type regeneration: it creates two tables and one function that the contract does not declare. The regeneration itself is blocked (CP-089, CP-092) and is not attempted. The exact specification of what regeneration must produce is handed to the operator in this manifest and in the task record, so a blocked regeneration is not mistaken for a schema that needs no types.

No `workforce_mix` of department scope is introduced here. The department entity and its authority boundary are 20260927100100's; this file only supplies the vendor identity a vendor DEPARTMENT will point at, through a composite foreign key that makes a cross-organization vendor reference structurally impossible.
layeredPlan: Layer 0 (preflight, read-only, operator). Run the Layer 0 queries and record every result. Four things decide whether this file is correct for THIS target: (a) `to_regclass('public.vendors')` and `to_regclass('public.org_vendors')` - if EITHER is non-null, STOP. Some other migration or an out-of-band apply has started resolving the merge question this file records as UNRESOLVED, and its post-condition will abort; re-derive the decision rather than proceeding. (b) `select role, perms from public.org_role_permissions order by role` - if any role carries vendor.view or vendor.manage, record it, because that changes who can read the new tables and DB-016's invalidation note applies to whoever seeded it. (c) `has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.organizations','select')` - if false, every policy in all three WFC-004 migrations denies, so stop and report rather than applying a change whose only visible effect is that workforce reads return nothing. (d) `has_schema_privilege('authenticated','auth','usage')` - same failure direction, and it is the dependency the self-keyed arms add.

Layer 1 (apply, single run, operator). One transaction, explicit, this file only - never `supabase db reset`, never `db push --include-all`, never a chain replay (CP-051). Two CREATE TABLE, five indexes, RLS enable+force on both, eight DROP+CREATE POLICY, four COMMENT ON POLICY, four COMMENT ON COLUMN/TABLE, the grant/revoke block, then a DO block that RAISEs unless: both relations exist as tables with RLS enabled AND forced; all eight policies exist on the right command, permissive, and are not anon- or PUBLIC-reachable; no policy carries an unconditional clause, branching on polcmd so a FOR INSERT policy's structurally-absent USING is not reported; each UPDATE policy's using and with check RENDER the same predicate; both same-organization composite foreign keys exist by name; and NEITHER `vendors` nor `org_vendors` exists. The post-condition is inside the same transaction as the change, so a target that cannot reach the asserted state fails the apply instead of reporting success. A CORRECT RESULT INCLUDES a failed apply caused by the last assertion, which means some other migration owns the vendor entity home and this file's recorded decision is out of date.

Layer 2 (postflight, read-only, operator). Run `psql -f supabase/tests/wfc004_workforce_departments_contract.sql`; expect ZERO violation rows and exactly one summary row rendering `WFC-004 workforce departments|t|0`. Then the labelled caller probes in postflight.queries, as at least FOUR different identities, because this table has no self-serve read path: an organization administrator (expected 0 rows, with the matrix gap stated), a member whose org_members.permissions array carries vendor.view (expected their organization's rows), a member of the OTHER organization (expected 0), and a revoked member (expected 0). A denial probe run as the wrong identity is not evidence. WHAT A CORRECT DENIAL LOOKS LIKE: `vendor_view` returning 0 for an org administrator is CORRECT today and is a provisioning gap, not a broken policy. The operator must not widen the matrix to make it non-zero; that is a WFC-003 decision under CP-102 and it invalidates every active acting-context session.

Layer 3 (no fourth layer in this lane). The unresolved vendors/org_vendors merge, the sixteen-value VendorCategory question, whether staffing_agencies are vendors, and the vendor.* matrix provisioning are all ROUTED rather than absorbed. None is required for this file to be safe, and folding any of them in would convert a bounded schema task into a product decision it is not sized for.

preflight.expectedAffectedRows: Zero pre-existing data rows are changed. Two tables and one table's indexes are created; RLS is enabled and forced on both; eight policies are dropped-if-present and created; grants are issued. No pre-existing relation, column, constraint, trigger or function is created, altered or dropped. The only rows this file writes are rows in the two NEW tables, and it writes none at apply time.

execution.resumeStrategy: Authored - manual apply pending (CP-051). One transaction, one file. Two CREATE TABLE take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock only on relations that do not yet exist, so there is no contention with a live table. CREATE INDEX on a new table takes no meaningful lock. DROP POLICY and CREATE POLICY take locks on catalog rows, not on any table's data. No table is rewritten, re-indexed or re-vacuumed, so there is no lock-budget risk from the data side. Safe to apply BEFORE any consumer change, and it is safe in the strict sense: it creates two relations that nothing reads, so no committed surface can lose a row it could previously reach. The behaviour that changes is that `vendors` and `org_vendors` STILL do not exist - nothing about the six degraded reader sites improves, because improving them requires the merge decision this file records as unresolved. The apply's one externally visible effect on an existing surface is NONE, which is exactly why it can be applied without a flag.
execution.idempotency: Deterministic and repeatable. `create table if not exists` for both relations, `create index if not exists` for all five indexes, `drop policy if exists` + `create policy` with a final name for each of the eight policies, `comment on` for each, an explicit grant/revoke block, and a DO block that only reads the catalog and RAISEs. Verified by applying the file FIVE times on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster in supabase/tests/wfc004_workforce_departments.harness.sh: the second through fifth applies produced no error, and the policy signature over both relations (8 policies with their commands) was byte-identical before and after, measured as a sorted concatenated string rather than asserted.

quarantine.strategy: No data movement, no backfill, no batch. The change is two relations, five indexes, eight policies and a grant block. There is no partial-application state: the file is one transaction and its own post-condition RAISEs if the asserted state is unreachable, so a half-applied policy set cannot be committed. The SIX chain-absent reader relations are NOT created by this file and are instead recorded as reviewable rows by 20260927100200, which is the whole point of the decision recorded above.
quarantine.lockBudget: has_perm is wrapped in `(select ...)` in every predicate so the planner evaluates the SECURITY DEFINER call as an InitPlan once per statement rather than once per row. Its own body is two lookups on org_members (primary key on (org_id, user_id)) and org_role_permissions (primary key on role), both indexed by their constraints. The `exists` conjunct is an index-only lookup on the organizations primary key. The added work versus a target with no vendor tables is the creation of the tables themselves.

constraints: vendor_entities_id_org_key UNIQUE (id, org_id) - not a logical key, it is the composite form PostgreSQL requires in order to reference (id, org_id) at all. It exists so that a merge, a vendor department and any future cross-relation reference can be proven to stay inside one organization by a FOREIGN KEY rather than by a predicate somebody can forget.

vendor_entities_merged_same_org_fkey FOREIGN KEY (merged_into_id, org_id) REFERENCES vendor_entities (id, org_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT - one organization per vendor entity, enforced as a constraint. `on delete restrict` rather than cascade: a merged row must never be silently deleted, because the alias history loses its target. This ratifies lib/admin/vendor-domain.ts:72-74,85 and lib/admin/vendor-identity.ts:302-304, which already refuse a cross-organization merge in application code; here it is a guarantee rather than a check.
vendor_entities_not_merged_into_self CHECK (merged_into_id <> id) - a self-merge is not a merge.

vendor_entities_legal_name_len / _display_name_len / _normalized_name_present CHECK (char_length(btrim(...)) between 1 and 240) - a vendor with an empty or unbounded name cannot be a dedup key, since normalized_legal_name carries the VEND-102 identity.

vendor_entity_aliases_vendor_same_org_fkey FOREIGN KEY (vendor_id, org_id) REFERENCES vendor_entities (id, org_id) ON DELETE CASCADE - an alias cannot name a vendor in another organization, so a name-match result can never leak across a tenant. Cascade here (unlike the merge FK) because the alias is subordinate: deleting a vendor legitimately removes its aliases.
vendor_entity_aliases_display_len / _normalized_present CHECK - an alias row is a dedup input, so an empty normalized value would be a silently useless row.

The two vendor tables' RLS policies ARE the authorization boundary. _select requires a non-null org_id that resolves to an organizations row plus vendor.view or vendor.manage; _insert, _update and _delete require vendor.manage, with _update carrying the IDENTICAL rendered predicate on using and with check so a caller cannot re-scope a row into an organization they do not manage. _select deliberately admits vendor.manage as well as vendor.view, matching DB-013's staff_members_scoped_read rationale (:153-157): a policy that lets an organisation manage its vendors but not read them is not a scope, and the historical repair for that gap in this codebase is to add a permissive policy, which is the defect.
indexes: vendor_entities_org_normalized_legal_uidx UNIQUE (org_id, normalized_legal_name) WHERE merged_into_id IS NULL AND status <> 'inactive' - PARTIAL, exactly as VEND-102 specified: an absorbed or inactive row must not block a new vendor from taking its name. The contract test asserts the predicate, not merely the index's existence, because an index that silently lost its WHERE clause stops being an identity guarantee while still being present.

vendor_entities_org_external_accounting_uidx UNIQUE (org_id, lower(external_accounting_id)) WHERE external_accounting_id IS NOT NULL AND merged_into_id IS NULL AND status <> 'inactive' - the second VEND-102 identity signal, and case-insensitive because accounting ids are supplied by the vendor.
vendor_entities_org_status_idx (org_id, status) - the vendor-governance reader's access pattern, and the shape a future org_vendors view would use if the merge is confirmed.

vendor_entities_org_normalized_idx (org_id, normalized_legal_name) - covered by the partial unique index for the same-org, non-merged, non-inactive case; kept for the merged/inactive rows the partial index excludes, so a search does not degrade into a sequential scan when a vendor has history.

vendor_entity_aliases_org_vendor_norm_uidx UNIQUE (org_id, vendor_id, alias_normalized) and _org_norm_idx (org_id, alias_normalized) - the first is the VEND-102 uniqueness on a retained alias, the second is the lookup an alias search performs.
vendor_entity_aliases_vendor_idx (vendor_id) - reading one vendor's alias history, which is what planVendorMerge does for the absorbed vendors.

That matters: the first revision of this file hand-wrote the summary as a second copy of eight predicates, the two drifted, and the postflight reported zero violations and `f` at the same time. The violation set is now materialised once into a temporary table and both the rows and the count read from it, so the summary cannot be a second opinion. recovery.rollback: DROP TABLE public.vendor_entity_aliases; DROP TABLE public.vendor_entities; - issued as a later forward migration, never as an edit to this file. recovery.forwardFix: Any correction is a new additive migration with a higher version carrying DROP/CREATE for these relations. Two forward-fix shapes are worth naming in advance. (1) If the vendors/org_vendors merge is CONFIRMED, the remedy is a column-limited VIEW named `org_vendors` over vendor_entities exposing only the columns its reader selects (`status` and the `org_id` tenant key) - not a second table, and not a rename. (2) If it is REFUTED, a second vendor master is needed and should be authored by the vendor-domain owner against an explicit column contract, not by widening this one. Note that a forward fix CANNOT accidentally inherit a name the 20260823210000 sweep exempts, because every policy in this file is named wfc004_* and matches none of the six exemption patterns; the contract postflight asserts that on a real target, and `node supabase/tests/wfc004_guarded_block_order.mjs --exemptions` fails if the chain's exemption list ever grows to cover them.

labelledProbes: PROBE 1, EXPECTED 0 ROWS, and this is a CORRECT result today: as an organization administrator with role `admin`, `select count(*) from vendor_entities` returns 0 because no role matrix row carries vendor.view. A non-zero result means someone seeded vendor.* into org_role_permissions; record who and when, because that write invalidated every active acting-context session (DB-016).

PROBE 2, EXPECTED their organization's row count and nothing else: as a member whose org_members.permissions array carries {vendor.view, vendor.manage}, `select count(*) from vendor_entities` returns the count for THEIR organization. This is the path that works today and it is the tenant-configuration half of WFC-003 §2.5.2. A zero here is a real problem and means the per-member array is not being unioned.
PROBE 3, EXPECTED 0: the same member of organization B reads 0 of organization A's vendor entities.

PROBE 4, EXPECTED 0: a REVOKED member reads 0, because has_perm filters on org_members.status = 'active' (20260821180438:139). A non-zero result means the target's has_perm is the pre-20260711153040 version, which did not filter on status, and the whole workforce RLS surface is fail-open - STOP and route to DB-002.

PROBE 5, EXPECTED 42501: a member with vendor.manage on organization A inserting a vendor row with org_id = organization B. The with check clause re-evaluates the permission against the row as it WILL exist.
PROBE 6, EXPECTED 23503 on vendor_entities_merged_same_org_fkey: a vendor in organization A with merged_into_id pointing at a vendor in organization B.
